UAE Pension Calculator for Emiratis (GPSSA)

Enter your date of birth, first registration date, planned end of service and average salary; the calculator picks the law that applies and estimates your pension.

Prepared and reviewed by the Mustahaqati team · Last updated: 2026-11-03

Estimate your pension

Decides the law: before or from 31 October 2023.
New law: average of the last 6 years. Old law (private sector): average of the last 5 years.

New law, 30 years at 55, average AED 17,500: 80.1% × 17,500 = AED 14,017.50.

This is an estimate; GPSSA sets the official pension. Expats in the private sector should use the gratuity calculator. Prefer Arabic? Use the Arabic version.

Frequently asked questions

How is the pension calculated under the new law 57/2023?

For those first registered from 31 October 2023: the pension salary is the average contribution salary of the last 6 years (72 months). The rate is 2.67% for each year up to 30 years (80.1%), then 4% for each year after that, up to 100%. The minimum pension is AED 10,000, with the government paying the difference.

When is the pension due under the new law?

On reaching 60 with at least 15 years of contributions, or on resignation after 30 years of contributions at age 55 or over, with no reduction. Mothers get a reduction in both conditions depending on the number of children.

How is the pension calculated under Law 7 of 1999?

For those registered before 31 October 2023: the average contribution salary of the last 5 years in the private sector, at 60% for 15 years plus 2% for each extra year, up to 100% at 35 years. A pension on resignation needs 20 years of contributions and the specified age.

How much is deducted from my salary for pension?

Under the new law, 11% from the Emirati employee and 15% from the employer, with the government covering 2.5% of the employer's share in the private sector for salaries under AED 20,000. Under the old law, 5% from the employee.

What if I resign before a pension is due?

An end-of-service gratuity is paid on the pension salary: 1.5 months' salary for each of the first five years, 2 months for each of the next five, and 3 months for each year after that, with at least one year of contributions.

Does it cover Abu Dhabi and Sharjah government employees?

No. Abu Dhabi private-sector employees fall under the Abu Dhabi Pension Fund and Sharjah government employees under a separate system, each with different rules.
